source.title: V2 exact packing evidence

metricDefinitions.label: Time saved
metricDefinitions.definition: 100*(1 - packed target elapsed / native fused target elapsed), paired by seed. Positive is faster. Includes setup and all preceding probes; first scheduled target crossing without interpolation.

metricDefinitions.label: Test difference
metricDefinitions.definition: Packed full WikiText-2 test BPB minus native fused full-test BPB. Lower is better; reused V1 corpus, regression evidence.

metricDefinitions.label: Intervals
metricDefinitions.definition: Two-sided 95% Student-t intervals across seven small-model or five larger-model paired seeds. Minimum mean time saving 10%; maximum upper quality difference 0.01 BPB.

caveats: One Apple M5 Pro, PyTorch 2.14.1 MPS, one corpus, two model sizes; desktop timing is not a controlled multi-device systems study.
Packing is an established systems technique; this is an authored implementation and measured application, not a claimed invention of parameter flattening or a new chain rule.
No CUDA, compiled-training, distributed-training, very large model or global state-of-the-art superiority claim.
Gradient/optimizer groups must be homogeneous and every parameter active. One additional dense gradient vector is allocated; activation memory and gradient matrix multiplications are unchanged.
Exactness means mathematical equivalence; floating-point reduction/optimizer order can change trained bytes and loss slightly.

WikiText-2 official validation/test were already evaluated by V1. V2 pilots use only the last 5% of training bytes; no official held-out result informed V2 packing or baseline selection. New frozen seeds provide a timing replication; test BPB is a reused-corpus numerical/quality regression check, not a fresh unseen-dataset generalization claim.

narratives.deck: An investigation into faster transformer training: a failed approximate backward, followed by exact gradient and optimizer packing against native fused AdamW.
narratives.findings:
## V1: adaptive sampling did not beat its baseline

Across five paired seeds, Cotangent's mean elapsed time reduction to 3.2 validation BPB was **-5.21 (95% CI -11.44 to 1.02)%**. Positive means faster; negative means slower. The predeclared minimum was 10%, with an interval above zero.

Final test degradation was **0.0089 (95% CI -0.0133 to 0.0311) BPB**. The quality gate failed against the 0.03-BPB margin. All primary pairs reached the target. The combined efficiency-and-quality gate failed.

All **36 planned runs completed**, representing **141,312,000 predicted training bytes** across the campaign. The result applies to this measured setup, not to all existing backpropagation methods.
narratives.controller:
## Spend accuracy where the gradient needs it

Cotangent audits each selected layer every 32 steps. An exact weight gradient estimates signal strength; row norms estimate the sampling second moment. The controller chooses a row budget for the next interval, bounded below by 64 rows. If its requested budget reaches 75% of all rows, ordinary native backpropagation is used on non-audit steps.

Activation gradients stay exact. Audit steps use exact weight gradients. The controller is a heuristic based on stale statistics; it does not certify the error of every intervening update.

Across recorded training steps in the small-model arms, the mean layer row fraction was **90.7%**. This is an unweighted diagnostic average at logging points, not a measured full-run FLOP reduction. Values of one include native fallbacks and exact audits. The behavior explains why quality preservation can leave little computation to save.
narratives.mathematics:
## The mathematical idea

For a linear layer, flatten the batch and sequence dimensions into N rows. Let X contain input activations and D contain output cotangents. The weight gradient is a sum of rank-one matrices:

`G = DᵀX = Σᵢ dᵢ xᵢᵀ`.

Draw k rows independently with replacement from probabilities pᵢ, then use

`Ĝ = (1/k) Σⱼ (dᵢⱼ xᵢⱼᵀ / pᵢⱼ)`.

Conditional on the model and batch, its expectation is the exact weight gradient before floating-point rounding. Its mean-squared Frobenius error is

`E‖Ĝ − G‖² = (Σᵢ ‖dᵢ‖²‖xᵢ‖²/pᵢ − ‖G‖²) / k`.

The variance-minimizing probabilities are proportional to `‖dᵢ‖‖xᵢ‖`; a 5% uniform mixture prevents zero support. The audit uses this expression to estimate k for a relative RMS error target of 0.5. The exact input gradient remains `dX = DW`.

This applies classical [randomized matrix multiplication](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0097539704442684) to training; importance sampling itself is established prior art. The project contribution is the tested controller, backend implementation, matched comparisons, and preserved evidence.

Even perfect removal of the weight-gradient multiplication leaves the forward and input-gradient multiplications. The arithmetic-only speed ceiling for that linear layer is 1.5×; attention, optimizer work, sampling, and audits reduce the end-to-end opportunity. Unbiased gradients do not imply unbiased AdamW updates after nonlinear clipping. [Full derivation and assumptions](https://github.com/atilavahedian/cotangent/blob/main/docs/MATHEMATICS.md).
narratives.study-design:
## A frozen, matched comparison

All arms train the same byte-level causal transformer on [WikiText-2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Salesforce/wikitext), starting from scratch. The main model has 3,346,944 parameters, four layers, width 256, sequence length 256, and batch size eight. Six methods run for 2,000 steps across paired seeds 11, 23, 37, 53, and 71. A 19,280,896-parameter, six-layer model compares native and adaptive backward for 1,500 steps across three paired seeds.

Native BF16 exact backpropagation is the primary baseline. Controls include exact custom backward, uniform 25% row sampling, importance 25% sampling, and a 25% Walsh–Hadamard sequence projection. The projection control changes activation gradients as well as weight gradients; it is inspired by [LBP-WHT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.15275), not an official reproduction.

Initialization, batch schedules, data, precision, AdamW settings, learning-rate schedules, and evaluation windows are matched. Every optimizer step synchronizes Metal. Elapsed time includes setup, data transfer, sampling, audits, clipping, optimization, resource checks, and validation probes.

Success was defined before held-out evaluation: every primary pair must reach 3.2 validation bits per byte, mean paired time reduction must be at least 10% with its 95% interval above zero, and the upper paired interval for final test degradation must be at most 0.03 BPB. Time is recorded at the first scheduled crossing, without interpolation. [Inspect the frozen protocol](https://github.com/atilavahedian/cotangent/blob/main/artifacts/frozen-study.json).
narratives.pilots:
## What changed during development

Only a held-out portion of the training split informed development. The first Metal optimizer attempt failed because forced foreach clipping was unsupported; that failure remains in the record. BF16 became the matched baseline after a precision pilot.

The initial adaptive implementation synchronized the CPU once per layer and was substantially slower. Batching audits into one transfer and bypassing sampling when the controller selected dense computation removed most of that overhead. The final source and protocol were frozen after these revisions. The table shows the revised one-seed diagnostic pilot, not final superiority evidence.
narratives.limits:
## What this study can establish

This is a local experiment on one corpus and one Apple M5 Pro with 24 GiB of memory. It does not establish performance on CUDA, billion-parameter models, distributed training, or other tasks. Five primary seeds and three larger-model seeds provide limited statistical evidence, and serial desktop timing can vary with the environment.

The scheduled quality probes cover the first 65,536 validation bytes; the final validation and test evaluations cover their complete splits with fixed, non-overlapping contexts. Bits per byte is not directly comparable to word-token perplexity.

The method retains full activations and exact activation gradients, so it makes no activation-memory reduction claim. [INSTANT](https://github.com/hieu-trannn/INSTANT) targets gradient and activation compression; [APOLLO](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.05270) targets optimizer-state memory. Neither is directly reproduced here, so this report cannot claim to beat those methods.

The larger model's three-seed descriptive comparison showed **-11.91 (95% CI -34.99 to 11.17)%** time reduction and **-0.0122 (95% CI -0.1568 to 0.1325) BPB** final test difference.
narratives.reproduce:
## Inspect and reproduce

The [public repository](https://github.com/atilavahedian/cotangent) contains newly written research code, mathematical notes, tests, diagnostic failures, the frozen protocol, raw JSONL curves, and per-run summaries. Commits record protocol design, implementation, development measurements, optimization, and the freeze as separate milestones.

No code, trained weights, data preparations, or results were inherited from the author's previous projects. Training used local hardware only. The report interface uses the general-purpose Data runtime.

Follow the repository instructions to download the pinned dataset, verify the derivatives, rerun the frozen campaign, and recompute its conclusions. Dataset content is not redistributed; its source license remains separate from the MIT research implementation.

The final integrity audit checked all 36 expected runs, matching paired initialization and batch schedules, frozen source and data-manifest hashes, full held-out evaluation coverage, raw-curve/summary consistency, and every checkpoint's SHA-256. These checks verify evidence consistency; they do not convert a failed efficiency gate into a success.
narratives.curves:
## Equal work does not guarantee equal learning

Each point is the mean of five scheduled official-validation probes. These plots show the complete frozen training budget, including unsuccessful fixed compression controls. The time plot averages elapsed time and quality at corresponding optimizer steps; the primary effect estimate uses individual seed crossings in the table above, not crossings interpolated from these mean curves.
narratives.packing-findings:
## V2 did not meet its frozen win criteria

Across **seven paired seeds**, the 3.35M model saved **9.62 (95% CI 5.71 to 13.54)%** elapsed time to the same 3.2-BPB target. Training-step time fell **12.62 (95% CI 12.15 to 13.08)%**. Final full-test change was **0.0056 (95% CI -0.0034 to 0.0145) BPB**; positive means worse. Its predeclared tolerance was 0.01 BPB. The combined small-model gate **failed**.

The 19.28M model's **five paired seeds** saved **18.21 (95% CI 11.22 to 25.19)%** time to target, with **-0.0091 (95% CI -0.1526 to 0.1343) BPB** test change. Its combined gate **failed**. All **24 frozen runs completed**, consuming **88,064,000 predicted training bytes**.

The supported gain comes from exact gradient/optimizer layout on this backend. The original adaptive-sampling experiment below remains a negative result. This is a scoped training-efficiency result against an existing optimized baseline; it does not establish a new universally superior backpropagation algorithm.
narratives.packing-method:
## Keep the derivatives. Change their layout.

The model still runs full native forward and backward. Each parameter remains an independent autograd leaf, sharing storage with a slice of one contiguous master vector. After backward, Cotangent concatenates the complete gradients once, performs one global clipping norm, and applies fused AdamW to that vector. The concatenation and every device synchronization are charged to training time.

Write `θ = concat(θ₁, …, θL)` and `g = concat(g₁, …, gL)`. Because `‖g‖² = Σₗ‖gₗ‖²`, global clipping gives the same coefficient. AdamW's moment recurrences, bias corrections and weight decay operate coordinate by coordinate, so concatenation commutes with the update when every coordinate uses the same hyperparameters and step count. The forward function and chain rule stay unchanged.

This is exact in real arithmetic. FP32 norm reductions and fused kernels can reorder arithmetic, so the final trained bytes may differ. Eight-step CPU double tests compare gradients, norms, clipped/unclipped updates and both AdamW moments at 2e-14 tolerance. Actual-model MPS checks cover FP32 and BF16; the initial bitwise-equality assertion failed at 4.66e-10 absolute gradient difference and remains in the record. Numerical checks passed.

The method reduces optimizer tensor count and norm reductions; it adds one dense gradient vector and makes no activation-memory or derivative-matrix-multiplication saving. Parameter flattening is established prior art, including [PyTorch FSDP](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/distributed/fsdp/_flat_param.py). This is an implementation and measured application, not a new chain rule. [Proof, assumptions and code](https://github.com/atilavahedian/cotangent/blob/main/docs/PACKING.md).
narratives.packing-design:
## A stronger baseline and a separate freeze

Training-only diagnostics compared PyTorch's automatic, foreach and fused AdamW, plus packed automatic/fused variants. Native **fused AdamW** was the fastest unmodified option in those pilots and is the final control. Both final arms use native exact autograd, BF16 autocast, FP32 parameters and the same model, initialization, batch schedule, clipping, optimizer settings and learning-rate schedule.

Seven fresh paired seeds train the 3.35M model for 2,000 steps; five fresh pairs train the 19.28M model for 1,500 steps. Pair blocks are shuffled in advance and native/packed order is balanced. Every step synchronizes MPS. The target clock includes setup, batching, full backward, packing, clipping, AdamW, checks and preceding scheduled validation probes.

The predeclared win requires all pairs to reach 3.2 validation BPB, at least 10% mean paired elapsed-time reduction with its two-sided 95% Student-t interval above zero, and the upper paired full-test difference at most **0.01 BPB**. The larger-model gate is evaluated separately. Missing target crossings stay censored.

WikiText-2 validation/test were already seen during V1. No official held-out result informed V2's implementation or optimizer selection; this is openly a reused-corpus quality regression check with new timing seeds, not a fresh-dataset generalization claim. The result is bounded to this Apple M5 Pro, this PyTorch MPS version, these two models and this corpus. CUDA, compiled or distributed training and global state-of-the-art superiority are untested. [Frozen V2 protocol](https://github.com/atilavahedian/cotangent/blob/main/artifacts/v2/frozen-study.json).
